appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise, qui faisait la grimace quand on la traitait de cuisinière, avait pour le valet de pied qui disait, en parlant d'elle, « la gouvernante », la bienveillance spéciale qu'éprouvent certains princes de second ordre envers les jeunes gens bien intentionnés qui leur donnent de l'Altesse.
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise is flattered by being called 'la gouvernante' instead of 'cuisinière' and rewards the young footman with special favor, but the narrator frames her pleasure through an ironic comparison to minor princes craving the title 'Altesse,' which gently mocks her status-consciousness even as it registers a real local elevation.

status_effects.explanation: Within the household hierarchy, Françoise gains a modestly elevated title and secures the footman's deference, though the narrator's satirical comparison to petty princely vanity qualifies the elevation as somewhat comic.

ambiguities: The flattering address ('la gouvernante') is spoken in-scene by the unnamed young footman, but the passage's governing evaluative act is the narrator's ironic simile comparing Françoise to minor princes; source is attributed to the narrator to reflect this layering rather than a direct character-to-character exchange.
